claims.claim: SBG V3 detects semantic changes better than static SBG V1
claims.caveats: CIs overlap; V1 is a weak baseline

claims.claim: SBG V3 contains behavioral information beyond execution volume
claims.evidence: Phase 1: exc_frac AUROC=0.567 > SBG V3 AUROC=0.540
claims.caveats: This is the central negative finding

claims.evidence: Phase 2: detection rate 7.5% on 173 integer mutations
claims.caveats: Hard mutations undetectable; easy mutations partially detected

claims.claim: SBG V3 is invariant under function rename (SP-2)
claims.caveats: Fixed entry-fn bug; residual invariance failure persists

claims.evidence: Phase 3: DEV=0.488, VAL=0.512, TEST=0.546 — high variance

claims.claim: V3 features (call bigrams, input sensitivity) add information
claims.evidence: Phase 8: no_all_v3_features delta=-0.001; call bigrams delta=+0.002

claims.claim: Benchmark labels are valid (EQUIV/CHANGED correctly assigned)
claims.caveats: 65 load failures; 35 oracle FN; oracle uses limited inputs

claims.evidence: Phase 9: SBG=0.546 > AST-hist=0.429; v2 reference AST=0.553 > SBG v2=0.531
19/19 unit tests pass; validated against sklearn; WMW tie-aware

claims.claim: SBG can detect real regression bugs
claims.caveats: N=8 is too small; but direction is clearly negative
